tldr: Headlines across all 12 country buckets lead with security and military framing — deadly clashes, IDF operations, funerals — with near-universal convergence on the basic casualty count. The agency attribution fractures sharply: Jerusalem Post's 'terror shooting' inverts the perpetrator logic found in pan-Arab and Turkish headlines characterizing settler actions as raids, arson, and 'pogroms.'

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to use the term 'terror shooting,' assigning a terrorism label to the Palestinian actor — all other outlets describe the same event as a 'clash,' 'shooting,' or 'confrontation' without applying criminal-law categorization.

Only headline to carry the UN Special Rapporteur's 'pogroms' characterization, introducing an international-law accountability frame in the title that appears in several body texts but is suppressed from almost every other outlet's front-page heading.

Only headline to foreground Palestinian fear ('Fears for Palestinians') as the primary emotional register rather than a symmetrical casualty count, attributing agency unambiguously to 'settlers' as killers.

Only outlet to pivot the headline entirely away from the West Bank settler confrontation, instead covering Israeli strikes on Hamas in Gaza — redirecting readers to a different conflict theater and erasing the settler-violence story from the headline.

Only outlet to headline Netanyahu's order to establish new settler outposts as the lead consequence of the clash, surfacing the territorial-expansion dimension that Israeli and Western outlets buried or omitted from above-the-fold presentation.

bottom_line: At headline level this is a security-escalation story everywhere, with the consequential frame divergence — who bears criminal responsibility — detectable only through specific lexical choices: 'terror shooting' (Jerusalem Post) versus 'settlers raid / kill / set fire' (pan-Arab, Turkish, and Israeli liberal outlets), a distinction most readers absorb as background noise rather than contested framing.
